Specifically, the compound is a target of 21-Hydroxy-Ent-Isozonarone, (1R,4S,5R,9S,10R,13S)-5-(hydroxymethyl)-5,9-dimethyl-14-methylidenetetracyclo[11.2.1.01,10.04,9]hexadecan-13-ol, and Lycorenan-7-one,9,10-dimethoxy-1-methyl-. These compounds are known to interact with Prohibitin, indicating a possible pathway through which the compound may influence Prohibitin activity. The evidence is consistent across different pathways, suggesting a potential mechanism involving the interaction of the compound with Prohibitin through multiple intermediate targets. The strength of the evidence is moderate, with varying scores across the paths, but the shared target of Prohibitin across multiple compounds supports a plausible relationship. The exact mechanism of interaction remains uncertain, and further experimental validation would be needed to confirm the direct relationship between the compound and Prohibitin.
